title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A refractory high-entropy alloy, likely composed of elements such as Nb, Mo, Ta, W, etc.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Investigation or manipulation of chemical short-range order (CSRO) within the alloy, possibly via annealing or computational modeling.
recollection.structure: Guess: The alloy exhibits regions of CSRO, meaning local atomic arrangements deviate from random mixing.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: CSRO reduces phonon scattering compared to a fully random alloy, allowing higher phonon heat conductivity.
recollection.results: Guess: The main quantitative result is an increase in phonon thermal conductivity in the alloy with CSRO, compared to a random solid solution; the paper likely quantifies this increase and discusses implications for thermal management in high-entropy alloys.

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies manipulation of chemical short-range order and local nonrandom arrangements, without the Monte Carlo protocol, HfTi/TiZr clusters, B2-like ordering, or percolation pathways. It correctly recalls reduced phonon scattering as a conductivity-enhancing mechanism, but omits reduced lattice distortion, high-frequency phonon DOS changes, and the competing precipitate-scattering effect. No quantitative value is provided; the actual increase is about 12%.
